sentences.text: In 2023, Poland's ruling party won the most votes, and still lost power. How?
Who can vote? Polish citizens from 18, at home or abroad.
For the Sejm, parliament's main house, you put one cross next to one candidate.
Parties above 5% share the seats by votes, and their most popular candidates get them.
These 460 MPs make the laws and vote the government in.
The Senate, one winner per district, can amend laws, but the Sejm has the final say.
In 2023, Law and Justice came first, but without a majority.
The next three parties teamed up, voted down its prime minister, and elected Donald Tusk.
And the president? Elected by the people for five years, in two rounds if needed. Karol Nawrocki won in 2025.
He can veto laws, and overriding him takes three fifths of the Sejm, more than the government has.
Should the party with the most votes always get to govern?
